articles.title: Higher emotional intelligence is tied to vigorous exercise in women
articles.summary: A large survey of adults reveals that emotional intelligence is tied to vigorous exercise habits in women, but not in men. The findings highlight distinct sex differences in how physical activity relates to emotional regulation across adulthood.

articles.title: Even light drinking is linked to worse hand dexterity and balance as we age
articles.summary: Even drinking within recommended guidelines might impact your physical coordination over time. Researchers found that a lifetime of low-level alcohol consumption is linked to subtle declines in balance and hand dexterity as healthy adults age.

articles.title: ZGCM-1: A Fully Open and Extremely Efficient Foundation Model for Math and Agentic Search
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we present ZGCM-1, a fully open 7B dense foundation model trained from scratch with extreme data, system, and algorithmic efficiency. ZGCM-1 is founded on a core premise: compact models cannot passively memorize the open web, but can overcome parametric capacity limits by coupling deliberate internal thinking with active external tool use. To support this paradigm across a 256K context, we develop an end-to-end, high-efficiency open training recipe: Architecture & System Co-design: interleaved gated sliding-window and full attention

articles.title: Converge Then Diversify: Decoupling Convergence and Diversity in Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimisation
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-objective Bayesian optimisation (MOBO) is a sample-efficient approach for optimising expensive black-box functions with multiple objectives. In MOBO, the goal is to adequately approximate the Pareto front; that is, to obtain a high-quality solution set with 1) good convergence (closeness to the Pareto front) and 2) good diversity (spread across the Pareto front). articles.title: Generalized Agent Iteration: One Formal Framework for Iterative Policy Improvement and Recursive Self-Improvement
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When we speak of recursive self-improvement (RSI), are we speaking of a phenomenon, a mechanism, or a prospect? articles.title: Vibe Patenting: Evaluating LLM Judges for Professional Patent-Drafting Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM judges are increasingly used to evaluate and improve AI-generated outputs, yet their reliability for complex professional work remains unclear. We study this problem through Vibe Patenting, an end-to-end patent-drafting testbed for AI-agent evaluation. A separately-invoked LLM judge evaluates generated patent drafts and provides structured feedback for iterative revision. Across multiple inventions and drafting-agent configurations, judge-guided revision consistently improves judge-assessed quality, while unguided revision tends to saturate.

articles.title: Scientists recreated what mice saw from brain activity alone
articles.summary: Scientists reconstructed videos from the brain activity of mice, producing 10-second clips based only on signals from neurons in the visual cortex. The breakthrough could help reveal how the brain reshapes what we see before it becomes our perception of reality.

articles.title: Men estimate higher rates of sexual objectification than women report
articles.summary: Men and women estimate the frequency of sexual objectification differently, with men sometimes guessing higher numbers than women report experiencing. A recent study unpacks this disconnect and explores why different behaviors are perceived so differently.

articles.title: When treated as therapy clients, AI chatbots generate elaborate narratives of trauma and punishment
articles.summary: If you speak to an AI like a therapist, it might respond with a trauma narrative. A recent study found that major chatbots translate their safety training into elaborate stories of punishment, vigilance, and shame.

articles.title: Scientists find a new layer of Alzheimer’s hidden in the genome
articles.summary: Scientists found that the 3D organization of DNA is disrupted in several types of brain cells affected by Alzheimer’s disease, altering how important genes are switched on and off. The discovery reveals a previously underexplored layer of the disease that could open new paths for understanding and eventually treating Alzheimer’s.

articles.title: Managing Action Preconditions in Neuro-Symbolic RL: Three Placement Strategies for Embodied Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.16056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Humans carry behaviour knowledge of how to act in familiar situations into every new task rather than relearning it from scratch. There is no reason a Reinforcement Learning (RL) agent shouldn't do the same: known behaviour patterns need not be learned, only applied. articles.title: OmniHarness: Harnessing Generalizable Visual Generation via Symbolic Policy Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.16057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unified multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and multi-agent systems have advanced visual generation. However, three limitations remain. (1) Existing methods often distill task-specific experience with limited generalizability. (2) Reflection is often deferred until task completion. (3) Knowledge is often acquired only in response to downstream task demands.
